beats.intro: Chapter nine, lesson four. Glycolysis. [[cube]]Drop a sugar cube into water, and it comes apart. [[map]]In a cell, the first stage of respiration does something like that to glucose. Here is our respiration map again. [[lit]]Glycolysis is lit: the first stage, out in the cytosol, before the mitochondrion. [[push]]Let's push in, and follow one glucose.
beats.overview: [[name]]Glycolysis means splitting of sugar. It takes one glucose, six carbons, and breaks it into two pyruvate, three carbons each. [[cyto]]It all happens in the cytosol, and it needs no oxygen. [[phases]]Its ten steps fall into two phases. First, the energy investment phase, steps one to five, where the cell spends two {{ATP|A T P}}. Then the energy payoff phase, steps six to ten, where it earns that back, and more. [[strip]]Here are the ten steps as a strip. You don't need to memorize the names. Just know what each phase does.
beats.invest: [[s1]]Step one. The enzyme hexokinase takes a phosphate from an {{ATP|A T P}} and puts it on glucose, making glucose six-phosphate. [[trap]]That charged phosphate makes the sugar more reactive, and it traps the sugar inside the cell. [[s2]]Step two rearranges it into fructose six-phosphate. Still six carbons. [[s3]]Step three. Phosphofructokinase spends a second {{ATP|A T P}}, adding a phosphate to the other end. [[key]]This is a key step for regulating glycolysis. We will meet it again in lesson nine. [[bill]]So far the cell has only spent. Two {{ATP|A T P}} are gone, and nothing is earned yet.
beats.q1: Quick check. What does the first phosphate do for glucose?
beats.split: [[cleave]]Step four is the split that gives glycolysis its name. The enzyme aldolase cuts the six-carbon sugar into two different three-carbon sugars. One is glyceraldehyde three-phosphate, or {{G3P|G three P}}. The other is dihydroxyacetone phosphate, or {{DHAP|D H A P}}. [[count]]Count the carbons: six becomes three plus three. Nothing is lost. [[iso]]Step five, an isomerase, turns {{DHAP|D H A P}} into {{G3P|G three P}}, and it keeps going, because {{G3P|G three P}} is used as fast as it forms. [[two]]So from here on, there are two {{G3P|G three P}}, and every payoff step happens twice. That is why the slide writes a two in front of each molecule.
beats.q2: Quick check. What does aldolase make?
beats.payoff: [[s6]]Step six is where energy shows up. Each {{G3P|G three P}} is oxidized: it gives its electrons to {{NAD+|N A D plus}}, which becomes {{NADH|N A D H}}. A phosphate is attached, and the product is rich in energy. Two molecules, so two {{NADH|N A D H}}. [[s7]]Step seven. That phosphate moves straight onto {{ADP|A D P}}, making {{ATP|A T P}}. This is substrate-level phosphorylation: an enzyme moves a phosphate from a substrate directly to {{ADP|A D P}}. Two molecules, two {{ATP|A T P}}. [[s8]]Step eight shifts the remaining phosphate along. [[s9]]Step nine, enolase, removes water, and makes phosphoenolpyruvate, which holds a lot of potential energy. [[s10]]Step ten. Pyruvate kinase moves the last phosphate onto {{ADP|A D P}}. That is substrate-level phosphorylation again, two more {{ATP|A T P}}, and the product is pyruvate. Two of them.
beats.yield: [[made]]Now add it up. The payoff phase formed four {{ATP|A T P}}. [[used]]The investment phase used two. [[net]]Four made, minus two used, leaves a net of two {{ATP|A T P}}. [[nadh]]There are also two {{NADH|N A D H}}, carrying four electrons for later. [[pyr]]And there are two pyruvate, with two water molecules. [[co2]]Count the carbons: six went in, and six came out, in two pyruvate. No carbon dioxide is released in glycolysis. [[o2]]And no oxygen was used, so glycolysis runs with or without it.
beats.example: Let's try numbers. [[ten]]Suppose a cell breaks down ten glucose. Each uses two {{ATP|A T P}} and forms four, so ten glucose use twenty, and form forty. [[net10]]The net is twenty {{ATP|A T P}}. [[nadh10]]And twenty {{NADH|N A D H}}, two for each glucose.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[s1]]Glycolysis splits glucose, six carbons, into two pyruvate, in the cytosol, with or without oxygen. [[s2]]The investment phase spends two {{ATP|A T P}} and splits the sugar. The payoff phase makes four {{ATP|A T P}}, and two {{NADH|N A D H}}. [[s3]]The net is two {{ATP|A T P}}, two {{NADH|N A D H}}, and two pyruvate, with no carbon dioxide. [[end]]Now try the practice.
